death.note: Stated as a century and never recorded. This folder’s own life says the page «puts the story in the seventh century», the story being Nikodemos the Hagiorite’s synaxarion of the cobbler who gave half his earnings to the poor; 601–700 is that century, and the century is all that is taken.

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 17 Νοεμβρίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. The line enumerates its two members, so John gets a folder of his own and the two relate each other, on `docs/CORPUS.md` §10.1. The page is an account rather than a life: John saw Zacharias the cobbler coming out of the church of Hagia Sophia accompanied by divine light, followed him home, and learned that although married he lived in virginity and chastity, that he gave half of what he earned by his craft to the poor, and that he had lived a life dear to God — «(7ος αι. μ.Χ.)». Of John it says that he was rich and an officer, that he despised worldly things and lived a simple and ascetic life, frequenting the churches every day, where he happened to meet Zacharias. The page then quotes Nikodemos the Hagiorite's synaxarion at length, where Zacharias tells how he divides his wages in two, the first and chief part to Christ in his poor brothers, and how he fled his house afterwards to escape the bait of human glory. **No `dates` proposed**: the «7ος αι.» is a century for the account and the corpus's practice in this wave has been to take a century the page states — but here the page attaches it in a parenthesis to the story and not to either man, so nothing is recorded and the century is in the prose. No `locations` and no hymn. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence on the life page.
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue as printed by pravoslavno.rs (25 September 2026).
